evidence.quote: PROCYON leverages natural language as the unifying modality to bridge knowledge domains and represent arbitrary protein phenotypes.

representation_rationale.summary: Natural language is used to connect knowledge domains and represent arbitrary protein phenotypes.

evidence.quote: PROCYON is not constrained by controlled vocabularies or pre-defined terminologies of protein function, and can generate openended phenotype descriptions beyond those seen during training.

representation_rationale.summary: The representation supports open-ended phenotype generation beyond predefined vocabularies and training phenotypes.

evidence.quote: However, even advanced large language models (LLMs) [23] learn only from text-based associations, typically derived from biomedical literature
and cannot incorporate non-textual protein data, such as atom-level protein structures.

representation_rationale.summary: Text-only LLMs learn text-based associations and cannot incorporate non-textual protein data such as atom-level protein structures.

evidence.quote: sequence- and structure-based methods rely on pre-defined functional categories for prediction, limiting their ability to generalize to phenotypes not yet codified in controlled ontologies and pre-defined vocabularies of protein function.

representation_rationale.summary: Sequence- and structure-based categorical approaches are described as limited in generalizing to uncodified phenotypes.

evidence.quote: A related limitation is PROCYON's static training dataset, which is unable to leverage continually generated biological research

representation_rationale.summary: The static training dataset cannot incorporate continually generated biological research.
